findings.title: Interpolating queries before the $__range exclusion check breaks splitting-safety for $__range queries
findings.body: runSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on every target (lines 296-299) before partitioning them with querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() (lines 282-287, 300). isQueryWithRangeVariable() is meant to detect the literal `$__range` token in the raw expr and exclude such queries from splitting, because (per the existing comment) the interpolated $__range value would be wrong once the query is split into sub-ranges. After this change, the expr passed to isQueryWithRangeVariable() has already had `$__range` substituted with the actual duration computed from the *original, unsplit* request range. The literal token is gone, so the check can no longer detect these queries, and they will now incorrectly be treated as splittable. Each split sub-request will then execute with a baked-in range window from the full request instead of the correct per-chunk window, producing wrong/duplicated aggregation results for any query using $__range. This directly contradicts the rationale documented in the adjacent comment and is a data-correctness regression introduced by moving interpolation to the top of the pipeline.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice when shard splitting delegates to runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables() (lines 49-53) before sharding. Later, splitQueriesByStreamShard()'s runNextRequest() builds subRequest.targets from these already-interpolated targets (via interpolateShardingSelector) and passes them into runSplitQuery() (line 163 in the full file). runSplitQuery() itself unconditionally calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on every incoming target (querySplitting.ts, the new .map() at the start of runSplitQuery). This means each query is run through template-variable interpolation twice per shard group. Besides being wasted work (tested in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts as 5 calls to applyTemplateVariables for a single logical query across 4 shard groups), this is risky if applyTemplateVariables is not fully idempotent (e.g. if it unconditionally injects ad-hoc filters/label matchers into the selector), since a second pass could duplicate filters already baked into the expr by the first pass. The test suite only exercises this with a trivial mock replace() that happens to be idempotent, so it does not actually validate correctness of double interpolation against the real datasource implementation.

findings.title: No test covers that $__range queries remain excluded from splitting after the interpolation reorder
findings.body: The PR adds a test only for interpolation of $__auto/$step before execution, but does not add or update any test exercising a query containing the $__range variable to verify it is still excluded from splitting (querySupportsSplitting/isQueryWithRangeVariable). Given that interpolation now happens before this exclusion check (see querySplitting.ts), and the check relies on finding the literal `$__range` token in the expr, this is exactly the scenario most likely to regress from this change, yet it is untested.
